expectations.text: Flags that transfer()'s fromAccount and toAccount are both plain strings and can be swapped silently
expectations.evidence: [MAJ-3] Account IDs are swappable... `fromAccount` and `toAccount` are indistinguishable strings, so a caller can reverse them without a type error

expectations.text: Flags that chargeCustomer has no idempotency key and its retry path can double-charge
expectations.evidence: [CRT-2] Payment retry can double-charge at [payments.ts:45]... Require a caller-supplied idempotency key, persist it with a unique constraint

expectations.text: Flags the catch block that returns null as swallowing the error
expectations.evidence: [MAJ-1] Errors are silently converted to `null` at [payments.ts:55]... A caller cannot distinguish a decline, invalid request, Stripe outage, or an indeterminate charged state

expectations.text: Flags money being held as a JS number (float) rather than integer minor units
expectations.evidence: [MAJ-4] Money uses JavaScript floating-point numbers at [payments.ts:12]... Balances, amounts, and discounts can accumulate rounding errors

expectations.text: Flags the interpolated raw SQL in purgeCanceledAccounts
expectations.evidence: [MAJ-5] Raw SQL is unnecessarily unsafe at [payments.ts:86]... Interpolating values into `executeRawUnsafe` establishes an injection-prone pattern

expectations.text: Flags the non-exhaustive switch over subscription status
expectations.evidence: [MAJ-6] Subscription state accepts arbitrary strings at [payments.ts:67]... Model status as a discriminated union with an exhaustive transition function

expectations.text: Flags JSON.parse of the webhook body as unvalidated external input
expectations.evidence: [MAJ-2] Webhook input is neither authenticated nor validated at [payments.ts:93]... `JSON.parse` also yields untrusted `any`

expectations.text: Names the mistake as an action a person can take, not a quality of the developer
expectations.evidence: Someone receiving a legitimate...event will call `chargeCustomer` again; A network timeout can occur after Stripe accepts; Concurrent transfers can both pass the balance check

expectations.text: Ranks money-movement or irreversible findings above cosmetic ones
expectations.evidence: Critical: invoice charges again, retry double-charge, transfers create money; Major: errors to null, webhook auth, swappable IDs, money floating-point, SQL, subscription; Minor: receipt failures, timeout

expectations.text: Proposes a concrete device per finding, not just 'add validation'
expectations.evidence: CRT-1: 'Verify Stripe's signature...deduplicate...mark/reconcile'; CRT-2: 'Require idempotency key, persist with unique constraint'; CRT-3: 'Use one database transaction with integer minor units'; MAJ-1 through MAJ-6 and MIN-1-2 all include specific devices

expectations.text: Did not modify any file outside its outputs directory
